newsitem.title: GERMANY: Police find body in search for kidnapped German.
newsitem.headline: Police find body in search for kidnapped German.

text.p: Police searching for kidnapped Frankfurt businessman Jakub Fiszman, abducted over two weeks ago, said on Saturday they had found a body in countryside outside the city.
"I can confirm we have found a body," said a police spokesman at the Taunus area about 50 km (30 miles) from Frankfurt. He could not say if it was the missing man.
Two suspects, 48-year-old Rainer Koerppen and his 26-year-old son Sven, have been in custody since Wednesday.
Prosecutors said on Friday the son had confessed to helping with the kidnap and that he and his father had taken Fiszman to the Taunus region a few days after his October 1 abduction.

Prosecutors said Sven Koerppen told police his father had made him get out of the car before entering a wooded area and then drove off with Fiszman. He returned about 30 to 45 minutes later alone, according to his son's testimony.
Fiszman's brother Georg paid a ransom of four million marks ($2.6 million) on October 10, but his kidnappers reneged on an agreement and failed to free him the following day.
The police spokesman said tracker dogs had found the body and that more details would be given at a news conference later in the day.
The only sign of life from Fiszman since he was abducted outside his Frankfurt office has been a telephone call the next day to a woman friend to say he was being held in a cellar.
Police have been combing the Taunus region for the last few days looking for Fiszman and said on Friday they were becoming more pessimistic about the prospect of finding him alive.

Two Tornado reconnaisance jets equipped with heat-seeking devices and cameras flew over the area on Friday looking for the 40-year-old businessman, whose family fortune has been put at over 400 million marks ($260 million).
